experience_themes.why_this_theme: The bounded corpus contains repeated evidence around portable execution, artifact identity, promotion, runtime delivery validation, and controls introduced after delivery defects.
experience_themes.what_the_experience_suggests: SAGE has meaningful engineering experience in preserving delivery provenance and using validated controls to reduce rebuild or generated-helper ambiguity.
limits: This is an LLM synthesis of a bounded corpus, not a general competence claim.
Current runtime readiness is not established by historical delivery evidence.

experience_themes.why_this_theme: Lessons and later actions repeatedly emphasize reconciling actual external state, retrieving prior failure experience, and avoiding stale continuation assumptions.
experience_themes.what_the_experience_suggests: When execution diverges from expectation, SAGE has accumulated useful experience favoring observed-state reconciliation and evidence-guided correction over mechanical replay.
limits: The evidence does not prove that every recovery can be automated.
Authority and material path changes can still require Architect re-entry.

experience_themes.why_this_theme: The corpus includes explicit causal-evidence and failure-attribution work together with retrospective evidence showing repeated correction costs before stronger controls existed.
experience_themes.what_the_experience_suggests: SAGE has accumulated experience turning failures, corrections, and completed objective evidence into reusable causal learning rather than treating execution history as disposable logs.
limits: One episode or one successful control does not establish general maturity.
The usefulness of a past lesson to a new objective still requires contextual judgment.

experience_themes.why_this_theme: The corpus contains runtime validation, guardrail, and observability evidence, although the current repository projection did not surface direct current zero-trust runtime proof.
experience_themes.what_the_experience_suggests: SAGE has relevant runtime-validation experience, but the available repository evidence should not be overstated as current zero-trust readiness.
limits: Executor-local runtime receipts are unavailable on this machine.
Historical runtime guardrail evidence is not equivalent to current external-access proof.

intent_applicability.why: SAGE-ACTION-20260815-002 explicitly addresses portable stage execution, artifact promotion, engine-neutral orchestration, and governed phasing, which overlaps materially with the current intent's portable-build and exact-promotion concerns.
assumptions: The current objective still uses comparable artifact identity and promotion semantics.
The current delivery target has not invalidated the prior execution assumptions.
unknowns: Whether the current cluster and publication path are presently ready.
Whether all runtime receipts needed for the proof are available from this executor.
intent_applicability.implication: Reuse the proven artifact/provenance constraints as a starting prior, but revalidate them against the current target before execution.

intent_applicability.why: The retrieved repository evidence demonstrates runtime validation and guardrail experience, but it does not directly establish the present zero-trust external-access state; executor-local runtime receipts are unavailable here.
assumptions: Past runtime-validation patterns are still useful for designing the current readiness check.
unknowns: Current cluster health and externally reachable workload state.
intent_applicability.implication: Treat prior runtime experience as design guidance, not proof; a small current-state readiness check has high information value.

intent_applicability.why: The retrieved lesson explicitly says to reconcile remote state before cohesive mutation and promotion, directly matching the current goal of avoiding unnecessary operator-mediated replay when external state has advanced.
assumptions: Recovery still crosses Git/GitHub or another externally mutable boundary.
unknowns: How much of the current end-to-end path will require recovery at all.
intent_applicability.implication: Prefer observed-state reconciliation and bounded correction over replaying stale mechanical steps.

innovation_beyond_experience.proposal: Use a meaningful first-party Human Participation change as the workload for the eventual end-to-end proof.
innovation_beyond_experience.why: It could make stakeholder value and delivery proof part of the same episode rather than spending effort on a disposable demo.

innovation_beyond_experience.proposal: Run only a bounded current-state readiness check before the full live episode if runtime uncertainty remains decision-relevant.
innovation_beyond_experience.why: This buys information about a possible blocker without turning the objective into infrastructure modernization.

innovation_beyond_experience.proposal: If current evidence contradicts a historical lesson, preserve the contradiction and let the newer objective context drive a revised path rather than forcing reuse.
innovation_beyond_experience.why: Accumulated experience should improve priors, not constrain innovation or freeze old architecture.

architect_authority: Architect decides objectives, trade-offs, and whether to transfer experience into action.
